verdict.justification: Deliverable A is preferred primarily because its Excel workbook is properly built as a dynamic, formula-driven tracker, whereas Deliverable B relies on static hardcoded numbers throughout its workbook. In a professional setting, receiving a spreadsheet where sums, lookups, and conditional statuses are hardcoded text and numbers (like B's `xl/worksheets/sheet2.xml:F28	2960` and `xl/worksheets/sheet3.xml:L5	Within range`) defeats the purpose of an Excel tracker. Deliverable A uses proper formulas (`SUMIFS`, `IF`, cross-sheet references, and an Assumptions tab) across all sheets. Additionally, on the analytical side, there is a slight ambiguity in the prompt regarding whether the 15% admin exclusion reduces the denominator (net project capacity, as A does) or only excludes admin hours from the numerator while keeping gross capacity as the denominator (as B does, which makes 85% the normal full-load project allocation rate and 90% an exceed-15%-reserve threshold). Notably, both A and B recognized this exact ambiguity and included the alternative calculation as a reference column in their tables, which shows great thoroughness from both; however, A's dynamic spreadsheet engineering and clean analytical presentation give it the clear edge.
